blindSummary:
The transgender soldier at the centre of the country's most-watched military-gender case lived and died in this state/province: aged 23, she was found dead at her home in its capital city on 3 March 2021 (apparent suicide) following a forced military discharge after gender-reassignment surgery and during ongoing mental-health counselling at a centre near her residence. Initial police and army handling classified the death as 'natural'; this was overturned only three years later (April 2024), when the defence ministry's central casualty review board recognised it as service-related. The wrongful initial classification is the evidence: an institutional denial of the connection between anti-trans policy and a trans person's death, corrected only after sustained advocacy.

The death is a single nationally prominent case; no repeat-violence data exist for this state/province. Documentation of its handling, and of the three-year correction, is what the dossier records here.
